chunks: Ali ibn Hassan from Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), so Mihzam entered upon him. Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'Call the maid for us to bring us oil and kohl.' So I called her, and she came with a flask of violet (oil). It was a day of intense cold. So Mihzam poured some of it into his palm, then said: 'May I be sacrificed for you! This is violet (oil), and this is the intense cold.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'And what is the matter with it, O Mihzam?' He said: 'Our physicians in Kufa claim that the violet (oil) is cold.' He (peace be upon him) said: 'It is cold in the summer, soft and hot in the winter.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the temperature of violet oil?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Shia scholarly appreciation for empirical observation over rigid theoretical classification, as Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects the Kufan physicians' static humoral diagnosis of violet oil. By noting that the oil feels 'cold' in summer but 'hot' and softening in winter, the Imam demonstrates the relativity of physical properties to environmental context, a nuance often overlooked in contemporary medical theory. This reflects the broader Imami tradition of valuing practical wisdom (*hikmah*) alongside textual and theoretical knowledge.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Hassan, from Abdul Rahman Bin Kaseer who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, so Mahzam came over to him<sup>asws</sup>. So Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said to me: ‘Call the maid for us<sup>asws</sup> to bring us<sup>asws</sup> the (massaging) oil and kohl’. So I called her with it and she came over with a flask of violet (oil), and it was an intensely cold day. So Mihzam poured in his hand from it, then said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! This is violet (oil), and this is extremely cold’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘And what is the matter with it, O Mihzam?’ So he said, ‘Our physicians at Al-Kufa are alleging that the violet (oil) is cold?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘It is cold in the summer, and is soft and hot in the winter’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Hassan has narrated from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Kathir who has said the following:

“Once I was with abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when Mehzam came to visit him (the Imam) and abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, said to me, ‘Call the slave-girl to bring for us oil.’ I called her, she brought a bottle of viola, and it was a cold day. Mehzam poured a certain amount on his palm, then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, this is viola and the day is very cold.’ He (the Imam) asked, ‘What about it, O Mehzam?’ He replied, ‘Our physicians in al-Kufah think that viola is of cold nature.’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is cool in summer and it is soft and warm in winter.’”
